⚡️🇷🇺🇺🇦 What appears to have come out of Russia's own “Pandora's box” is the Banderol — once a relatively scarce, Frankenstein-like cruise missile, now suddenly appearing in growing numbers across Ukraine. During the latest wave, monitoring tracked roughly 12–13 Banderols against Odessa alone, while additional missiles were repeatedly reported toward Kiev and its surrounding region, Zhytomyr and western Ukraine. At the same time, dozens of jet-powered Geran-4s were tracked across Ukraine, including groups attacking Kiev.
The precedent is not simply that individual Banderols can penetrate Ukrainian air defenses, but the scale, timing and targets of the campaign. As Ukraine faces severe pressure on its interceptor stocks, a formerly scarce and comparatively inexpensive cruise missile is appearing in double-digit salvos and across multiple regions. Meanwhile, the expanding strikes have hit railway and logistics facilities, warehouses, fuel infrastructure, drone-production facilities, ports around Odessa and energy infrastructure in and around Kiev — showing that President Putin's warning that Russia would retaliate against Ukraine's logistics and its “most sensitive economic sectors" is by no means an empty threat. If this tempo persists, Banderol alongside the expanding Geran-4/5 family could provide Moscow with additional mass to sustain precisely the greater number and intensity of strikes the Russian president has now publicly announced. All eyes on the Banderol.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
The U.S. Navy has publicly disclosed a previously unannounced AIM-424 Long Range Air-to-Air Missile (LRAAM), also known as the "Malice", revealing the weapon mounted inside the internal weapons bay of an F-35C Lightning II with an AIM-120 AMRAAM mounted on the bay door. The Navy describes the AIM-424 as its next-generation, long range air to air missile, intended to give Navy and Marine Corps aviators greater capability against advanced threats.
The internal carriage is particularly significant. Rather than simply adding another externally carried long-range missile, the AIM-424 appears to have been designed around the F-35's limited internal weapons-bay dimensions, allowing the aircraft to retain its low-observable configuration while carrying a substantially longer-range air-to-air weapon.
The missile is still associated with testing and development, and the Navy has released few technical details regarding its range, seeker, propulsion or intended employment. The available imagery does, however, show the AIM-424 being evaluated on both the F-35C and F/A-18E/F, indicating that the weapon is being considered across the Navy's carrier aviation force.
Source: https://www.dvidshub.net/image/9879420/aim-424-long-range-air-air-missile-lraam

events.text:
🇨🇳🏝 New artificial island strengthens China's defense perimeter in South China Sea
👉 In less than a year, China has transformed the submerged Antelope Reef into a sprawling 1,500-acre artificial island in the Paracels archipelago, TWZ reports.
🔴 The island has a 680-meter dock capable of berthing border patrol vessels and warships
🔴 Infrastructure includes a helicopter pad and administrative buildings, along with internal roads and seawalls surrounding the island
🔴 Two concrete plants are supporting ongoing construction, with grading for the 3-kilometer runway for both civilian planes and military aircraft about halfway complete
The island will become part of China's expanding [network of maritime outposts](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70579), reinforcing logistics, persistent surveillance, and control over the surrounding waters.
The new outpost sits approximately 160 nautical miles south of Hainan Island, home to two of China's aircraft carriers and a significant submarine force. Its location in the northern South China Sea makes it particularly valuable for regional defense and rapid response.
♦️ The island extends radar and electronic surveillance coverage across the northern South China Sea
♦️ It provides another dispersed airfield for military aircraft such as H-6 strategic bombers, offering operational flexibility in a highly contested area
♦️ Local infrastructure will serve as a protected bastion for [nuclear-armed ballistic missile submarines](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/64811) and could complicate maritime operations by other powers in the area
♦️ Reports indicate China is also exploring unmanned defensive networks to protect the island, with [AI-driven systems](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/58570) integrating aerial drones, unmanned surface vessels, and underwater robots into a coordinated three-tier defense structure 
The creation of a military base on Antelope Reef supports the [security of the Chinese mainland](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73244) by pushing the defensive perimeter outward, adding complexity to any potential adversary's operational planning. This is particularly significant in the context of the US First Island Chain strategy, which seeks to build up American military presence in the Pacific and bottle up China in its coastal waters, limiting strategic maneuverability.

events.text:
🤔 Failed Iran war exposed US Navy as teetering on edge of breaking point
The [US Navy](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/51339) has spent years operating beyond what its fleet, maintenance system, and crews can sustainably support. 
The US-Israeli failed war on Iran [magnified these weaknesses](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73465), reports the Military Times.
While President Donald Trump desperately peddles whims like plans for a new class of battleships to lead his ["Golden Fleet"](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67741) and demands a navy capable of simultaneously confronting Russia and China, the numbers simply do not add up.
➡️ The navy remains an 11-carrier force in a world its own planners have described as requiring 15 carriers. With USS Nimitz approaching retirement, that number could soon fall to 10
➡️ The USS Harry S. Truman and [USS Gerald R. Ford](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67347) are sidelined for maintenance after extended deployments
➡️ The Optimized Fleet Response Plan was supposed to balance deployment, training and maintenance in predictable 36-month cycles
➡️ Instead, it produced 33,700 additional days in maintenance backlog (2014-2019) with fewer operational ships 
The Iran conflict has turned these chronic deficiencies into immediate operational problems.
🔴 When [Iranian retaliatory strikes ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65777)damaged the navy’s logistics hub in Bahrain, the US shifted support operations to distant Diego Garcia - more than 2,000 miles from carrier groups in the Middle East
🔴 [Food](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/68765) orders then required 30 days notice - impossible under combat schedules - so crews scavenged whatever could be salvaged from oilers
🔴 Deployments stretched past endurance limits, the USS Abraham Lincoln spent roughly 250 days without a port visit, and reports surfaced of sailors [attempting to go overboard](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73343)
🔴 Sailor shortfalls compound every failure: a 2021 GAO review found the navy routinely assigned fewer sailors to ships than workload needed
🔴 The same review revealed only 14% of navy officers surveyed slept at least seven hours per night during deployment
The result is a force that continues to ask the same sailors and the same ships to do more with less, all to cater to [Trump’s outsized ambitions](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73474).
Meanwhile, the ‘adversaries’ that Trump frets about – [Russia](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/56828) and [China](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70989) - are steadily outpacing NATO naval power.

The facility was located at a civilian truck depot, raising questions about the use of civilian infrastructure for military purposes. 
Ukrainian media published images revealing that multiple trucks had special equipment for launching and storing attack drones. The footage, however, was quickly deleted by Ukrainian sources shortly after publication.

🔥 Russia pounds Ukrainian logistics as air defenses fail again
Russian forces launched massive missile and drone strikes on Ukrainian transport and port infrastructure overnight. 
Targets hit: 
📌 Darnytsa train depot in Kiev - used for maintaining and repairing locomotives transporting military equipment for Ukrainian forces
📌 Brovary logistics center in the Kiev region - a major Nova Poshta logistics hub, storing drone components
📌 Railway station in Razdelnaya and port infrastructure in Odessa and Chernomorsk - power outages followed the strikes
Ukrainian air defense systems failed to intercept any of the ballistic missiles, the country's own Air Force admitted, following news that Ukraine is [running low on interceptor missiles](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73442) as Russian strikes keep getting stronger.
